description: Exploratory global pathway implementing all pledged NDC targets; GCAM 6.0.
pathwayDescription:
The Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) develops reference climate scenarios to help central banks, regulators, and financial institutions assess transition and physical risks associated with climate change. The Nationally Determined Contributions, GCAM 6.0 (NDC GCAM) Scenario represents a policy-based pathway aligned with the implementation of countries’ current NDCs. It reflects the continuation of announced and planned climate policies without assuming additional or stronger measures beyond these commitments. This pathway incorporates targets through 2030, at which point ambition is assumed to be fixed.

The NDC pathway shows greater variation between underlying IAMs than most NGFS pathways due to different interpretations of the core set of input policies. It corresponds to an implied temperature rise of 2.5°C by 2100 for NDC GCAM, with GCAM forecasting only a 5% reduction in Kyoto greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions between 2020 and 2050, while the other IAMs model around a 50% reduction.

This scenario is one of seven scenarios published by NGFS. Note that all NGFS scenarios produced are using three different Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs): REMIND-MAgPIE, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM, and GCAM. These IAMs share the common assumptions that define each scenario, but may offer different projections based on underlying model structure. Technical users may wish to consult NGFS documentation to determine if a specific IAM best fits their applications.

coreDrivers.policies: Carbon price: the shadow carbon price reaches 33 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030 and 60 in 2050, the main lever moving investment and dispatch away from fossil fuels. Target technology shares: regional caps on coal-generation growth and limits on new nuclear and coal additions.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Emission constraints equal to pledged NDC targets (cut-off end-March 2024), with ambition held beyond the NDC horizon. GCAM applies these mostly as emissions constraints (Net Zero 2050 via exogenous GHG prices).
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: GCAM shares new investment by a logit on levelised cost, so cheaper options gain share without taking all. Exogenous declines (solar PV 2689 to 1021 US$2010/kW, 2020-2050, same in all scenarios) favour wind and solar: wind and solar reach 63% of 2050 generation (Current Policies 57%). With carbon at 60 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, the cost ranking tilts further to low-carbon options.
coreDrivers.investmentChange: Low-carbon power investment moves from 0.70% of GDP (MER) in 2020 to 0.96% in 2050, an increase of 37%. GCAM's GDP is exogenous, so the change comes from investment volumes.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Shared SSP2 v3.0 population and GDP drive energy and material demand: 9.59 billion people in 2050 and GDP (MER) growing 2.28%/yr over 2020-2050. The assumptions are common to all NGFS scenarios; GDP differs from Current Policies only through transition costs (-0.89% in 2050).

dependencies.dependency_description: Grid decarbonisation in Nationally Determined Contributions (GCAM) rests on the carbon price (33 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030, 60 in 2050). It lifts wind and solar from 13% of generation in 2020 to 63% in 2050 and cuts coal capacity to 73% of its 2020 level by 2040.

Power investment averages 734 bn US$2010/yr over 2025-2050 (1.13x Current Policies), including 571 bn/yr for grids, and must be financed. A 2050 carbon price of 60 US$2010/tCO2 erodes unabated fossil plant profitability.

With wind and solar at 63% of 2050 generation, grids, storage and flexibility must absorb variable output. GCAM adds backup costs for intermittent supply and reports no storage. Grid investment averages 571 bn US$2010/yr (2025-2050). No hourly dispatch is reported, so curtailment cannot be checked.
Power CCS captures 678 Mt CO2/yr in 2050 (677 Mt from bioenergy), so the pathway needs CCS at commercial scale; CCS cost differences between models drive large gaps in fossil generation.

GCAM uses graded renewable supply curves and allocates land by profitability. Power BECCS reaches 677 Mt CO2/yr and primary biomass 80 EJ in 2050, so land limits the negative-emission part of the power transition. Wind and solar at 63% of 237 EJ draw on the regional potentials.

GCAM balances water supply and demand by basin, including cooling-water use for power by technology, so water scarcity can raise thermal generation costs in Nationally Determined Contributions (GCAM). Physical climate damages are not fed back into the transition pathway.

Steel decarbonisation in Nationally Determined Contributions (GCAM) is steered only through economy-wide carbon pricing (60 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050) and emissions constraints; no steel-specific industrial policy is described. Steel emissions change by -58% over 2020-2050.

At 60 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, fossil ironmaking costs more, favouring electricity (5.9 EJ) and hydrogen (2.6 EJ) in steel in 2050. No steel investment or unit-cost data are reported, so financing needs cannot be quantified.

Hydrogen supplies 7% of steel final energy in 2050 in Nationally Determined Contributions (GCAM), so hydrogen production, transport and storage must reach steel sites. Economy-wide CO2 transport and storage investment is 111 bn US$2010/yr in 2050, none attributed to steel.

Hydrogen-based ironmaking must scale to 2.6 EJ (7% of steel energy) by 2050 in Nationally Determined Contributions (GCAM). It is not yet market-ready, and the documentation states no readiness or efficiency assumptions.

The only policy acting on aviation in Nationally Determined Contributions (GCAM) is the carbon price on transport fuel (60 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050); no aviation mandate such as SAF blending is represented. Passenger aviation goes from 6004 to 14308 bn pkm over 2020-2050.
Carbon-priced fuel holds 2050 passenger aviation to 95% of the Current Policies level (14308 vs 15033 bn pkm), so demand responds through price rather than fuel switching.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived Mt CO2 per EJ generated (1 EJ = 277.8 TWh). Scope 1 CO2 only; denominator is gross generation incl. CCS and bioenergy plants.

Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. CO2 only, Scope 1 (power-plant combustion, net of CCS); may include the electricity share of CHP. GCAM also reports Kyoto GHG for electricity.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. No storage capacity reported. Solar = PV + CSP; wind = onshore + offshore; CCS and non-CCS variants reported separately.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Gross secondary electricity (EJ/yr) by technology incl. CHP electricity; CCS and non-CCS variants reported.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived generation shares; storage excluded (not a generating technology).
Overnight capital cost per kW by technology (fossil, CCS, nuclear, renewables). No O&M, fuel or LCOE values.

granularity: By tech, part of value chain
byMetric.scopeLimitations: Annual investment, billion US$2010/yr. Post-processed variants may contain multi-model-average infill (NGFS Climate Scenarios Technical Documentation V5.0 (Nov 2024), p.82); native series used.
No lifetime values published; lifetimes fixed by technology, retirement endogenous. Inference relies on the coal capacity trajectory.
Derived t CO2(e) per t crude steel (sector emissions / Production|Steel, Mt/yr); primary and secondary routes combined; Scope 1 only.
Iron and steel modelled as one sector; ironmaking and steelmaking not separable. Kyoto GHG (GCAM); Scope 1, excludes purchased electricity. Process-emission treatment not stated.
Passenger-km (Energy Service|Transportation|Passenger|Aviation, bn pkm/yr); no freight or belly-freight split; domestic and international combined.
